headline: Revenue and profit surge on AI data-center power demand
summary_short: Bloom Energy's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose to $1.065 billion (+41.9% q/q, +165.5% y/y), with gross margin expanding to 33% and net income attributable to common stockholders of $196.3 million versus a $42.6 million loss a year earlier.
summary_long: Revenue jumped 165.5% y/y and 41.9% q/q to $1.065B, led by product revenue (+215.4% y/y) tied to a large AI-infrastructure customer deployment and Brookfield joint-venture projects. Gross margin expanded to 33% from 27% y/y on manufacturing efficiency gains, automation, and a $37.4M tariff recovery, partly offset by higher warranty costs. Opex rose $62.7M y/y, mainly stock-based compensation and scaling-related consulting costs, but revenue growth outpaced it, lifting operating income to $182.2M. Net income attributable to common stockholders was $196.3M versus a $42.6M loss a year earlier; effective tax rate stayed near 0.7% on a full U.S. deferred-tax valuation allowance. Cash from operations was $300.0M for H1 FY2026. No forward guidance range was stated in this 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: Company attributes the increase primarily to higher product revenue from stronger demand for its power solutions, including a significant deployment for a large AI-infrastructure customer and multiple projects executed through the Brookfield joint venture.

Company cites lower material, labor, and overhead costs from manufacturing efficiency improvements and automation, plus a $37.4M recovery of previously paid import tariffs, partially offset by higher product warranty costs.

Revenue growth outpaced a $62.7M rise in operating expenses, which the company attributes mainly to higher stock-based compensation and consulting/professional-services costs for scaling its solid oxide platform and AI data-center programs.

Company reports a $14.3M y/y increase in interest income from higher invested cash balances following its 0% convertible-note refinancing, plus an effective tax rate held near 0.7% by a full valuation allowance against U.S. deferred tax assets.

Company frames results around surging AI data-center power demand via its Oracle partnership and Brookfield joint venture; it separately disclosed rejecting a July 8, 2026 short-seller report on supply-chain sourcing via an 8-K furnished July 9, 2026.
